title: One step too far
hook: Loop one index past the end of an array. Who tells you?
concept: Reading outside an array is a mistake in every language, but the languages disagree on how loudly they complain. A loud failure is easy to find. A quiet one ships.

worlds.js: Reading past the end returns undefined, and 6 + undefined is NaN. A negative index is just a missing property, so [-1] is undefined. No error in either case.
worlds.python: The out-of-range read raises IndexError. Negative indexes are a feature that counts from the end, so [-1] is correct.
worlds.java: Both reads throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Loud, and therefore easy to find.

fix: Loop with i < length (or iterate the elements directly) and use at(-1) in JavaScript or length - 1 in Java for the last element.
